notes.meaning: The people cross the lake to Capernaum and find Jesus in the synagogue. They are puzzled because no boat was left for Him the evening before, so they ask when and how He arrived. Instead of answering their curiosity, Jesus focuses on their spiritual condition.

Jesus speaks with solemn authority to expose why the crowd followed Him. They were not drawn by the true meaning of His miracles, which showed He came from God, but merely wanted another free meal to fill their stomachs. He challenges them to look past earthly appetites to the real purpose of His coming.

Jesus warns the crowd not to spend their lives striving only for physical food that quickly spoils. Instead, they must seek the spiritual food that leads to eternal life, which He freely gives. God the Father has placed His seal of approval on Jesus through His holy life and mighty signs, proving He is the true Savior.

Taking Jesus' mention of work literally, the people ask what good deeds they must perform to please God and earn this blessing. Like many others, they assume that eternal life must be bought by human effort or ritual obedience.

Jesus corrects their misunderstanding by redirecting them from a long list of religious duties to a single necessity: trusting in the One God has sent. Faith in Jesus is not a wage earned by human power, but the root work through which a sinner receives God's grace.

The crowd asks Jesus for a miraculous sign to prove His authority, despite having just witnessed the feeding of thousands. They compare Him to Moses, arguing that Israel's ancestors were fed with heavenly manna every day for forty years. By quoting Scripture about this gift, they challenge Jesus to match or exceed that miracle if He expects them to believe Him.

Jesus corrects their view of Jewish history. Moses did not create or give the manna; it came from God the Father, and it only fed physical bodies from the lower skies. Now the Father offers the genuine, soul-nourishing bread directly from the highest heaven.

The true bread of God is a divine Person who descends from heaven to bring spiritual life. Unlike the ancient manna, which was given only to Israel for earthly survival, this heavenly bread imparts eternal life to the whole world.

Still thinking of physical bread that would keep them from ever starving again, the listeners ask Jesus for an unending supply. Like the Samaritan woman at the well who asked for living water without understanding what it meant, they desire the benefits while missing the spiritual reality.

Jesus clearly declares that He Himself is the bread of life. Coming to Him and believing in Him mean the same thing, and those who trust in Him find complete and lasting satisfaction for their deepest spiritual needs.
Jesus confronts their persistent unbelief. They had seen Him in person, heard His truth, and witnessed His miracles, yet their hearts remained hard and doubtful.

Even though many reject Him, Jesus assures His listeners that God's plan cannot fail. Everyone whom the Father gives to the Son will come to Him in faith, and Jesus gives the comforting promise that He will never turn away or reject anyone who comes.

differ.view: Those given to the Son are the elect chosen by God before time, and they are drawn by irresistible grace so that none will fail to come.
The Father gives to the Son all who feel their need of salvation and willingly yield to His drawing grace, which anyone can resist or accept.

notes.meaning: Jesus explains that He stepped down from heaven on a divine mission, not to pursue private human ambitions, but to carry out the Father's plan of redemption. Because His desire is completely one with the Father's, He will unfailingly protect and save all who are entrusted to Him.

The Father's commission is that Jesus should not lose a single person given into His care. His saving work guards the believer through every trial and finishes on the last day with the bodily resurrection to eternal glory.

differ.view: Christ guarantees that every true believer is eternally secure and can never finally fall away or be lost.
God desires every believer to be kept safely, but individuals must freely persevere in faith rather than turn away like Judas.

notes.meaning: Jesus states the open offer of the gospel for all people. Whoever looks upon the Son with sincere faith receives eternal life right now and will be raised up by Christ at the final judgment.

The Jewish hearers begin to mutter among themselves in offense because Jesus claims to be the heavenly bread. Their grumbling mirrors the complaint of their ancestors who murmured against God's manna in the desert.

They reject His claim of heavenly origin because they know His earthly family. Since they regard Him merely as Joseph and Mary's ordinary son from Nazareth, their familiarity blinds them to His true divine identity.
Jesus commands the crowd to stop their quiet complaining. He refuses to water down His message, showing them that the real problem is the stubborn unbelief in their own hearts.

Human beings are naturally helpless to come to Christ on their own because of sin. A person can turn to Jesus in saving faith only when the Father draws the heart, and everyone who comes will be raised up on the last day.

differ.view: God's drawing is an effectual and irresistible call granted only to the elect, creating a willing heart where there was only spiritual deadness.
God draws sinners by His Holy Spirit and loving invitations, enabling all to believe, though human beings can resist this grace.

notes.meaning: Quoting Isaiah, Jesus reminds them that under the new covenant, God's people will be directly taught by the Lord. This divine instruction is an inward work of the Holy Spirit on the heart, and whoever genuinely listens to the Father and learns from Him inevitably comes to Jesus.

Jesus clarifies that learning from the Father does not mean seeing God face-to-face with human eyes. Only the Son, who has His eternal origin with the Father, possesses direct sight and full knowledge of God, making Him the only One who can truly reveal Him to us.

With a solemn guarantee, Jesus summarizes His message: the person who places their trust in Him possesses eternal life right now. It is not just a distant promise for the future, but a present reality received through faith in the Son.
